images.title: Subtract a negative start
images.purpose: Show that going from Floor −2 to Floor −1 needs a button of +1, which is target − start.
images.composition: One vertical lift shaft centred with a short upward arrow, wide white space either side.
images.exact_structure: One vertical shaft with 5 equal floor lines, evenly spaced, labelled +1, 0 (grey #6B7280 ground line), −1, −2, −3 top to bottom. A teal #0072B2 dot at floor −2 (start) and an amber #E69F00 dot at floor −1 (target). One reddish purple #CC79A7 upward arrow between them spanning exactly 1 floor. Exactly 5 floor lines, 2 dots, 1 arrow.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
an arrow longer than 1 floor, or an arrow pointing down
images.takeaway: Target minus start still gives the button, even below ground.
images.description: A lift shaft with a start dot at Floor −2, a target dot at Floor −1, one short upward arrow labelled +1, and (−1) − (−2) = +1 below.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say which way the lift moves and how many floors, then read the subtraction.

image_decisions.why: The idea is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
